subject: Private deployment: rollback plan & ops brief following control-plane upgrade regression
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@horizonhealth.com>, Rajesh Patel <rajesh.p@medsys.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: [Incident] Control-plane regression after private node upgrade

Hi Emily / Rajesh —

Quick update from our side: during the 03:00 UTC rolling upgrade of private-control-plane nodes in the us-west-2 region we observed a regression in the control-plane handshake logic for some private deployments. That caused intermittent control-plane disconnects for 12 unique customer VPCs (including Horizon Health) between 08:45–09:03 UTC. We are classifying this as P2 given service degradation (longer model startup times, retry churn) but not persistent data loss.

What we know so far:
- Trigger: new handshake path introduced in 2027.05.02 build (controlplane v2.14.0).
- Impact window: ~08:45–09:03 UTC (successful automatic fallback restored most sessions after ~90s).
- Affected: private control-plane connections for a subset of long-lived agent handshakes at higher connection counts.

Immediate actions we are initiating:
1) Collecting full control-plane diagnostic traces and KV caches (attaching archive).
2) Preparing a rollback to the previous control-plane image (v2.13.7) if the canary shows instability. Proposed rollback window: 23:00 UTC tonight (2027-05-02) to avoid daytime traffic.
3) Pausing further automatic private-node upgrades until the root cause is confirmed.

Attachment: controlplane-logs-20270502.tar.gz (filtered diagnostics, handshake traces)

We want to confirm whether Horizon prefers an immediate rollback tonight at 23:00 UTC or prefers we keep the deployment on the current image while we run a targeted fix and a longer canary. If you prefer rollback, we'll run it as a rolling rollback with a canary on one AZ first and a pre/post health check.

Apologies for the disruption — our engineering lead (Laura) and I will own coordination and keep you updated every 30 minutes until resolved.

-David

David Kim
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@horizonhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, security@horizonhealth.com
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Incident] Control-plane regression after private node upgrade

Thanks, David. We saw elevated agent reconnects and a ~3–4x spike in start latency in our canary environment; patient queues backed up for ~5–10 minutes.

We are OK with a rollback tonight at 23:00 UTC as long as you provide:
- A clear rollback playbook and a one-page runbook for our SREs to verify health.
- A short postmortem with impact metrics (error counts, average startup latency before/during/after).
- Retention of the raw logs for 30 days for our security team to review.

Please include our security team (security@horizonhealth.com) on the postmortem. We'll plan to join a follow-up meeting — 16:00 UTC on Tue (May 4) works for us, otherwise later that day.

Emily Zhang
Head of Platform Ops, Horizon Health
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@horizonhealth.com>, Rajesh Patel <rajesh.p@medsys.io>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: [Incident] Control-plane regression after private node upgrade — rollback plan & ops brief

Emily — thanks for the quick response and for outlining requirements. We're aligned on the rollback tonight at 23:00 UTC. Below is the summary of the plan and asks from both sides.

Rollback plan (summary):
- 23:00 UTC start; rolling rollback of control-plane image from v2.14.0 -> v2.13.7 across 3 AZs.
- Canary on AZ-1 for 15 minutes with active traffic (Horizon will observe). If healthy, continue with 30-min pauses per AZ.
- Health checks: agent handshake success rate >= 99%, median model-start latency within 10% of baseline, no elevated 5xxs.
- Fallback: If canary fails, we will stop the rollback and promote a hotfix branch for validation; we will not proceed to full rollback without confirmation from both sides.

What we'll provide by EOD tonight:
- Rollback playbook (attachment: rollback-playbook.pdf).
- Postmortem outline and timeline for a full write-up (attachment: postmortem-outline.md).
- Persistent log archive retained for 30 days and shared via the Drive link below.
- A proposed SLA credit calculation for the impacted window (we'll include numbers in the postmortem).

Operational asks from Horizon:
- Confirm a single attendee for the 23:00 UTC run (on-call SRE + security watcher).
- Confirm acceptance of rollback if canary passes.

I'll run coordination from Redwood's side; David will be the exec on-call for technical actions and Laura will handle customer comms and postmortem.

Link to logs and runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-controlplane-logs

-Neha

Neha Kapoor
Director, Customer Reliability (Americas)
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@horizonhealth.com>, Rajesh Patel <rajesh.p@medsys.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-rollback update + invite for joint postmortem (INC-517)

Hi Emily / Rajesh —

Rollback completed successfully at 23:18 UTC last night; full rollback runbook executed with canary on AZ-1 and no residual instability observed in the us-west-2 region. Summary:
- Rollback start: 2027-05-02 23:00 UTC
- Canary pass: 23:15 UTC (15-minute observation window)
- Full rollback complete: 23:18 UTC
- Post-rollback result: agent handshake success rate returned to baseline; median model-start latency returned to within 3% of previous baseline.

What we published to the shared Drive: full control-plane traces, node-level metrics, KV-cache snapshots. See: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-controlplane-logs

We've opened internal ticket INC-517 for root-cause work and prioritized a hotfix PR to remove the non-deterministic handshake path. We'll share the draft postmortem by EOD Tue and schedule a joint postmortem meeting: proposed slot Wed, 2027-05-05 16:00 UTC. Please confirm availability.

Also confirming: we will retain the raw logs for 30 days and produce the requested impact metrics and an SLA credit estimate.

Attachments: postmortem-outline.md, rollback-playbook.pdf

Thanks for your patience. We'll treat this as a priority and ensure our release gating is updated to prevent similar regressions.

-Laura

Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@horizonhealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, security@horizonhealth.com
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 22:05:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Post-rollback update + invite for joint postmortem (INC-517)

Thanks, Laura — we appreciate the quick coordination and the thorough rollback. Confirming our team will join Wed 2027-05-05 16:00 UTC (Emily + one SRE + security). Please include the draft postmortem in the calendar invite when available.

Emily Zhang
Head of Platform Ops, Horizon Health
